comparison.objective: Candidate commissions and mechanically locks a robot-axis shock absorber through iterative impact testing; pr-1101 probes a duct to locate a blockage, marks its position, and withdraws the probe.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, setscrew unlocking/locking, collar fine-rotation, counterholding, bounded torque, and response-based tuning. pr-1101 requires advancing a long rod until obstruction contact, mapping that contact to an exterior marker position, marker placement, and rod withdrawal.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires physical unlock-adjust-relock operations and two repeatable ≥0.85 J cycles within specified velocity/stroke, rebound, overload, hard-stop, and drift limits. pr-1101 only states that the blockage must be found, marked above the duct, the rod removed, and released; it provides no numeric localization tolerance, contact-force/damage limit, withdrawal deadline, or hold duration, and has no spec versions.
comparison.reason: The tested abilities are meaningfully different: closed-loop dynamic damper adjustment and retention under repeated impacts versus contact-based blockage localization and spatial marking with a probe. Generic contact and object manipulation do not establish overlap, and pr-1101’s missing numeric rubric details do not plausibly make its objective equivalent to damper commissioning.
